newsitem.title: DUBAI: Two quakes hit southern Iran, no damage reported.
newsitem.headline: Two quakes hit southern Iran, no damage reported.

text.p: Two earthquakes jolted Iran on Monday, including one in the southern port city of Bandar Abbas, but there were no immediate reports of casualties or damage, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported.

It said a quake measuring 4.6 on the Richter scale shook Bandar Abbas at 8.03 a.m. (0433 GMT). The other quake measuring 4.2 degrees hit Izeh, a town some 800 km (500 miles) northwest of Bandar Abbas, 18 minutes later.

Bandar Abbas, which has 250,000 inhabitants, is a major commercial port on the Strait of Hormuz at the entrance to the Gulf. Iran's 8th oil refinery is due to be ready for operation in Bandar Abbas next month.
IRNA said there were no reports of damage or casualties from either quake.
A force four earthquake is powerful enough to cause heavy damage in a populated area.
Two strong earthquakes measuring 6.1 and 5.4 degrees on the Richter scale hit a mountainous region in northeastern Iran earlier this month, killing at least 79 people and injuring 260.
Earthquakes hit Iran regularly. The worst recorded one, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale killed 35,000 people in a densely populated area near the Caspian coast in 1990.
